statement.excerpt: In February, the day after Sora came out, I warned that it didn’t really understand physics—and wouldn’t — in essay called Sora’s Surreal Physics:
statement.document_title: Sora still appears to have trouble with physics

our_interpretation: The forecast concerns Sora and subsequent versions of that model family, with no stated deadline.
The plain reading of understanding physics is reliably generating physically consistent events across varied situations, including unfamiliar ones. It does not require flawless output.
The historical premise and the unlimited prediction are distinct. Evidence of existing failures cannot establish the prediction.
criteria.support_condition: Decisive evidence would have to establish an enduring inability of the relevant model family to achieve reliable physical consistency. Failures in finitely many versions provide provisional support only.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A later Sora version demonstrates reliable physical consistency and generalization across varied, independently evaluated situations.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent, reproducible evaluations showing a later Sora version reliably generalizing physical behavior across varied unfamiliar situations would contradict the forecast. Further failures alone would leave its unlimited horizon open.
